source.list: Naloxone Opioid Overdose Treatment: Evzio Criteria

criteria.text: Emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose manifested by respiratory and/or central nervous system depression.
Previous Narcan Nasal Spray use with documented intolerance OR a documented clinical reason why Narcan Nasal Spray cannot be used.

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Evzio (naloxone HCl) Criteria Version 1; Approved 1/22/2016; effective for dates of service 10/3/2016 and thereafter.
Dosage form/strength: Evzio Injection 0.4 mg/0.4 mL naloxone HCl auto-injector.
Evzio is intended for immediate emergency administration where opioids may be present and is not a substitute for emergency medical care.
Approval requires either Narcan Nasal Spray exception; denial is represented by failure of the any-predicate, not separate inverse OR denial clauses.
Authorization (notes only): initial up to 6 months; subsequent reauthorization up to 1 year.
Quantity limit (notes only): 1 box (2 auto-injectors) per fill.

Mechanism (notes only): naloxone competes at opioid receptor sites and reverses opioid effects including respiratory depression, sedation and hypotension, as well as psychotomimetic and dysphoric effects of agonist-antagonists such as pentazocine.

Overdose background / CDC guidance (notes only): guidelines recommend opioid antagonist access for patients at high risk of overdose; prescribers should consider offering naloxone when an opioid reversal agent is warranted. See source references for overdose management and risk factors.
